scripts.title: Getting through the egg case
scripts.reason: Strongest link between an unusual biological mechanism and a concrete inspection lesson.
scripts.text:
Why would a wasp lay its egg inside a cockroach’s egg case?

An ensign wasp is putting her young beside its food. But getting through that case takes work.

She braces herself against it and pushes in a slender egg-laying organ. The University of Florida describes this step as usually taking 15 to 30 minutes.

She leaves one egg inside. The larva that hatches has pointed jaws with small teeth for cutting through the individual cockroach eggs.

American cockroaches, one of this wasp's hosts, leave their egg cases in cracks and crevices. So when you inspect those warm, damp hiding places, look for egg cases as well as live roaches.

Helping you understand pests. Deep Six Pest Control.

scripts.title: Recognizing the wasp
scripts.reason: Useful identification details explain the visitor and lead to a practical inspection step.
scripts.text:
Why would a wasp lay its egg inside a cockroach’s egg case?

That's an ensign wasp. Her young feeds on the cockroach eggs inside.

The adult has an unusual shape: a tiny abdomen perched on a thin stalk. It flicks that part of its body up and down like a flag. Ensign is another word for a flag.

This wasp is only about five to seven millimeters long, and it doesn't sting or bite people.

If you find one indoors, place small insect monitoring cards tight against walls under sinks or behind appliances.

Use the traps to check for cockroaches, and leave the harmless ensign wasp alone.

scripts.title: From egg to adult, inside the case
scripts.reason: A coherent visual story follows the wasp through feeding, pupation and emergence.
scripts.text:
Why would a wasp lay its egg inside a cockroach’s egg case?

The cockroach eggs feed a young ensign wasp, but the case also holds it while it grows into an adult.

The mother places one egg inside. When it hatches, the larva uses pointed jaws with tiny teeth to cut through the individual cockroach eggs.

After feeding and growing, it becomes a pupa inside the same case. It doesn't spin a cocoon.

The adult cuts a small, round hole with a jagged edge near one end of the case. So the insect emerging from a cockroach egg case may turn out to be an ensign wasp.

Helping you understand pests. Deep Six Pest Control.

scripts.title: Finding where roaches are active
scripts.reason: Specific trap-placement advice explains where to monitor and how catches guide inspection.
scripts.text:
Why would a wasp lay its egg inside a cockroach’s egg case?

An ensign wasp leaves one egg inside, where her young will feed on the cockroach eggs.

If you spot the adult indoors and want to check for roaches, start with small insect monitoring cards.

Roaches tend to follow edges. Place the cards directly against walls under sinks or behind the refrigerator, with the openings lined up along the wall.

Use several locations and compare catches. The traps work while you're asleep or away, helping show where activity is concentrated.

A card near an exterior door can also help detect outdoor cockroaches coming in. Keep checking the cards over time to see whether catches rise or fall. So start your inspection where the traps show the most activity.

scripts.title: Checking for roaches and their eggs
scripts.reason: Brief egg-case comparison and packing advice add practical prevention value, with a looser connection to the wasp story.
scripts.text:
Why would a wasp lay its egg inside a cockroach’s egg case?

An ensign wasp lays one egg there so her young can feed on the cockroach eggs. American cockroaches are among its hosts.

American females leave their egg cases in cracks or crevices. German females carry theirs until the eggs are ready to hatch.

Corrugated cardboard gives roaches hiding places, so remove unnecessary boxes after unpacking.

Before bags, boxes or luggage come through the door, check for both live roaches and their egg cases.

Helping you understand pests. Deep Six Pest Control.
